content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text does the thing K-S2 governs: it labels a verse-based point UNDERDETERMINED by treating the two father-references as qualifying/opening the verse.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.", "room": "A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. I weighed reading one: a two-sense verse cannot be open or UNDERDETERMINED because both senses stand; reading two: it may be UNDERDETERMINED when one sense qualifies another.", "why": "The judge marks the Luke 2:48-49 point UNDERDETERMINED on the ground that the phrase 'thy father' is qualified by 'my Father's business,' so it treats a two-sense verse as open, contrary to K-S2."}
